reasoning: The source combines a continuous floating cliff shell, dense central fortress, four landmark families, a volcanic horizon, liquid/effect layers, and a multi-stage mission hierarchy.
Fidelity depends on deep attachment ownership, visible route clearance, repeated masonry/iron/rune systems, independent PBR responses, and cross-view volume inferred from one source.
The approved 32-part Gauntlet inventory and mobile action-ready requirements place this at the ultra-complex tier.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Ultra-complex is required by the observed architectural density, 32 approved production entries, multiple motion/socket systems, seven material families, phone-scale fidelity requirement, and single-view occlusion risk.

definitionOfDone: At 390x844 the island reads immediately as the supplied Lava Labyrinth: one deep basalt island, continuous molten channels, a dominant narrow Crucible Citadel, connected maze walls, four legible gates and a warm ember horizon.
All 36 renderer-owned canonical tiles stay unobstructed; authored geometry never duplicates tile, token, reward, stop, boss or island-clear progression.
Hatchery, Habit, Mystery and Wisdom landmarks preserve footprint-stable L1-L3 additive builds with visible robot/tool/scaffold contact and no root transform scaling.

Forge the Four Firebridges uses canonical mission actions to collect eight Ember Cores, spends two per stage, raises four cumulative bridge meshes, then awakens the Arena without bypassing Arena victory.

Obsidian, worked basalt, black iron, aged brass, magma and ember glass remain materially distinct under neutral, grazing and reference-matched lighting; reduced motion freezes decorative motion without hiding state.

featureGroups.name: Floating island silhouette, depth, and route clearance
qualityCriteria: The island reads as one deep supported volcanic mass with stepped terraces, jagged underside, broad front lavafall cuts, and asymmetric cliff breaks.
The full canonical route remains visible and quiet at 390x844 with no terrain, wall, bridge, or landmark intrusion.
failureModes: flat disc or disconnected rock pile replaces the deep source silhouette
route, landmark doors, or token path are obscured
lavafalls start or end in mid-air

featureGroups.name: Crucible Citadel tower, connected maze, gates, and arena identity
qualityCriteria: A tall narrow keep dominates connected stepped curtain walls and buttresses embedded in a radial arena foundation.
Every gate is a physical throughpass with plausible rear volume; the fortress is not a stack of disconnected boxes or a one-camera facade.
failureModes: tower loses dominance or reads as a generic castle
maze walls are loose cuboids without connected courts
rear/profile collapses or gates are painted recesses

featureGroups.name: Landmark foundations, lava channels, and Firebridge attachments
qualityCriteria: Every landmark foundation is buried into one owned terrace collar and remains within its footprint through L1-L3.
Each Firebridge connects paired landings through declared hinge and chain sockets; the complete swept envelope clears route, gates, cameras, and all L3 shells.
failureModes: bridge pivots from its center instead of its hinge
chain endpoints separate or machinery intersects
construction robots enter landmark or route collision volumes

featureGroups.name: Obsidian, basalt, iron, brass, soot, and magma response
qualityCriteria: Dark mineral, worked stone, black iron, aged brass, soot, cooled crust, and molten cores remain visually distinct through independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, AO, and emissive channels.
Macro strata, meso masonry/chipping, and micro pitting/edge wear survive neutral and grazing light; emissive spill never replaces material response.
failureModes: all dark surfaces read as uniform glossy plastic
magma becomes flat orange paint or blows out adjacent form
one texture is aliased across unrelated PBR channels

featureGroups.name: Action-ready build, mission, interaction, and reduced-motion hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Named roots, pivots, sockets, colliders, focus anchors, part-picking/explode metadata, LOD groups, and disposal hooks cover every approved production part.
Mission state commits through the canonical mutex-protected action before cinematic playback; four bridge stages are monotonic, replayable, interrupt-safe, and save-compatible.
Resting, working, commissioning, ambience, and reduced-motion modes converge on the same settled geometry without moving board, token, camera, funded meshes, or hit targets.
failureModes: UI or presentation layer owns gameplay progress
prior mission stages disappear or repeat after interruption
reduced motion reaches a different state
click/explode part definitions disagree or required parts are fused

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
